screens.title: Discover the Rule
screens.layout: clean split-screen comparison with one large example on each side: USUALLY vs NOW
screens.visualAid: deep-green USUALLY panel and restrained lime NOW panel; no decorative stock image
screens.studentAction: compare the two examples and choose the correct rule
screens.teacherAction: collect class prediction, then reveal the two rules in place
answers: Use the present simple to talk about what we usually do.
Use the present continuous to talk about what we are doing now / around the present.
screens.presentationRule: reveal one rule at a time

screens.title: Sonia · Usually vs This Week
screens.layout: Sonia portrait/identity card centred between two large timeline zones; avoid tiny table
usualItems: study at home in the evening
not wear her best skirt every day
screens.studentAction: drag each activity into USUALLY or THIS WEEK, then build one sentence at a time
screens.teacherAction: Responses first; Check classification; Show answer reveals completed sentence in the same row
screens.fit: maximum five rows visible at once; no scrolling

screens.title: Sonia Calls Granny
screens.layout: phone-call interface with two speech columns and large inline answer boxes
sourceCorrections: I'm not going to school this week.
screens.studentAction: complete the conversation inline, then listen and check
screens.teacherAction: Show answer fills each blank in its original speech bubble; Responses remain available
screens.presentationRule: show dialogue in two balanced chunks rather than one dense screen

screens.title: State Verbs · Repair the Sentence
screens.layout: one incorrect sentence at a time, large type, with a correction field and STATE/ACTION decision chip
screens.studentAction: correct the sentence and classify the key verb
screens.teacherAction: review Responses, then reveal correction and short rule in place
answers: I don't believe you can fly a plane.
We think this CD is very expensive.
I don't understand what she's saying.
screens.visualPolicy: no generic job photo; use typographic grammar focus

screens.title: Match Questions & Short Answers
screens.layout: two-column matching board with four pairs per Part; large cards and strong spacing
screens.partPolicy: Part 1 = first 4 pairs; Part 2 = last 4 pairs
screens.studentAction: match each question to its short-answer pattern
screens.teacherAction: matched pairs lock after Check; Show answer completes unmatched pairs
screens.responseBoard: record final pair mapping for each student

screens.title: Ask, Answer & Check
screens.layout: large rotating prompt card + 30–45 second round timer; minimal visual clutter
modelFrames: Do you play volleyball? — Yes, I do.
Are we speaking Italian? — No, we aren't.
screens.studentAction: ask one prompt, answer naturally, then mark peer accuracy
screens.teacherAction: Timer + Responses for quick reflection; no fake auto-score for speaking
screens.interactionUpgrade: rotate prompts instead of displaying all questions at once

screens.title: Quick Exit Check
screens.layout: five compact challenge cards revealed one by one
screens.studentAction: complete one final mixed response per target area
screens.teacherAction: Responses summary first; Show answer/model only after class review
screens.visualPolicy: text-led with small purposeful icons only; no repeated photo wall

globalRules.visualDirection: modern, premium, natural-light photography only when image materially supports the task
